name: avatar
title: Avatar
description: Who something belongs to — a monitor's owner, an alert's assignee — as a picture or as initials.
docs: Who something belongs to — a monitor's owner, an alert's assignee — as a picture or as initials. ```tsx // initials, when there is no picture // a machine's name works the same way ``` | prop | default | notes | | --------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | | `alt` | — | required; a **name**, and it becomes the initials | | `src` | — | omit it, or let it fail, and the initials are used | | `size` | `md` | `sm` 24px, `md` 32px, `lg` 40px | | `color` | `neutral` | `Button`'s five | | `isPreviewable` | `false` | opens the avatar large in a modal; it becomes a button | ## The fourth component with nothing to copy `pulse-replica/` has no avatar, no user chip and nothing person-shaped at all — after the date picker, the accordion and the toast, this is the fourth component here invented rather than replicated. So every decision comes from the system's own language: - **Square.** The sheet squares off its controls and makes exactly two exceptions, the checkbox's 2px and the radio's circle. A round avatar would be a **third**, so it is `rounded-none`. This is the one place a designer expects a circle, which is why it is stated rather than left to look like an oversight. - **A fill carrying `ink`**, like every other filled control: black on the luminous dark-theme accents, white on the deep light-theme ones. The five colours are literally `Button`'s table, so an avatar cannot drift away from the palette it sits beside. - **Mono, uppercase, letterspaced initials** — the face every other label here wears. ## Initials are derived, and the edges are checked The first letter of the first and last words, or the first two letters of a single word: | `alt` | initials | | ----------------- | -------- | | `Ada Lovelace` | `AL` | | `Ada B. Lovelace` | `AL` | | `fra1` | `FR` | | `" "` | `?` | A middle name does not change it, because the surname is what distinguishes two Adas. A name with no letters at all still has to render something, so it gets `?` rather than an empty box — the one case where the fallback invents rather than derives. A generic silhouette was the alternative and was rejected: it says "somebody", and in a monitoring system _which_ somebody is the entire content of the cell. ## A broken image falls back to initials, not to nothing `onError` swaps the `` for the initials. This is not an edge case — an avatar URL that 404s, a service with no picture, a directory that has not synced — it is the state a real dashboard spends most of its life in, and the failure mode of not handling it is an empty box. `BrokenImage` is a story with a source that cannot load, and it asserts the initials appear and the `` is gone. ## The name is announced once The wrapper is `role="img"` with `aria-label={alt}` and the inner `` is `alt=""`. Giving both a name announces the same person twice; giving only the image one leaves the initials case — the majority case — with no name at all. The `Default` story asserts the picture **actually arrived** by checking `naturalWidth`: an `` in the DOM proves nothing on its own, because a 404 leaves one behind. ## `isPreviewable` changes the element, not the styling ```tsx ``` Off — the default — this is a ``, a picture the tab order correctly skips.
